Competitive Intelligence

1.1

Generative Search

Cited answers to natural-language questions
Recommended for you

Generative Search is an AI-powered research system that answers complex business and financial questions through a conversational interface.

More about this feature

It picks the relevant parameters out of your question to run the most effective search, and every summarized insight cites the passage it came from.

Verifiable citations
Select any insight to open the source document with the passage highlighted. AlphaSense also checks that each cited snippet supports the claim.
Follow-up and related questions
Ask follow-ups in the chat bar without losing context, or pick a suggested related question to explore a new angle.
Show all results and copy
See every document behind the answer, or copy the full summary with its citations to your clipboard.
Best for
Company deep dives, industry research, change-over-time questions and comparables.

Step by stepPick a level

  1. Ask a plain-English question Novice
    Name the company, market or topic and what you need to know.
  2. Review the research plan Novice
    Check the plan before it runs so the answer covers the right ground.
  3. Verify two or three citations Novice
    Select a cited insight; the source opens with the passage highlighted.
  4. Ask one follow-up Intermediate
    Use the chat bar or a related question to go one level deeper with full context.
  5. Show all results Intermediate
    Open every document behind the answer and copy the summary with citations.
  6. Engineer the prompt Expert
    Add task, entity, time frame, sources and output format for a sharper answer.
  7. Hand off the work Expert
    When the job has several steps, pass it to a Workflow Agent or SuperAnalyst.

1.2

Generative Grid

Many questions across many documents, as a table
Recommended for you

When asking questions one at a time isn't enough, Generative Grid asks several natural-language questions across many documents at once and lays the answers out as a table.

More about this feature

Documents go in rows, questions go in columns, and every cell is cited.

Ask across hundreds of documents
What concerns are mentioned? What guidance is given? What did management say about macro effects? What are they saying about pricing?
Templates
Start from a gallery template, then edit, add or delete question columns.
Cell-level citations
Click any cell to open the passage behind the answer.
Grid Automation
The grid updates itself when new documents match its criteria.
Go deeper in courseworkAutomating Your Research With Generative GridCovers a full walkthrough.
Open course

Step by stepPick a level

  1. Create a new grid Novice
    Open Generative Grid and click New Grid.
  2. Pick a template Novice
    For example Earnings Analysis, Company Primer or Expert Interview Synthesizer.
  3. Add documents Novice
    Select companies, a watchlist or a document set, or pull documents from a Workspace.
  4. Customize the columns Intermediate
    Edit the template questions or add your own (your role's columns are below).
  5. Check cells against sources Intermediate
    Open the cited passage behind any answer before you use it.
  6. Add a category column Intermediate
    Force a short answer (Positive, Neutral or Negative) so the grid can be sorted and counted.
  7. Switch on Grid Automation Expert
    Let the grid keep adding new matching documents as they arrive.

Workspaces

Project spaces that keep context
Recommended for you

Workspaces are dedicated project spaces for organizing conversations, files, instructions and outputs around one initiative.

More about this feature

Rather than a one-off prompt, a Workspace is a persistent, context-aware environment that grounds AlphaSense's answers in the documents you choose.

Bring your own content
Upload or connect internal documents and curate external documents from the AlphaSense library.
Integrated AI tools
Chat with your curated set using Generative Search, or interrogate each document with Generative Grid.
Organization and recall
Save outputs, view past chats and activity, and add documents as the research grows.
Go deeper in courseworkCentralizing Your Workflows with WorkspacesOrganize projects, documents and chats in one place.
Open course

Pro tipUse one Workspace per project so you never rerun a search to get the same data.

Step by stepPick a level

  1. Create a Workspace Novice
    Name it after the project, client or question.
  2. Add documents Novice
    Upload internal files and save relevant AlphaSense documents and summaries.
  3. Chat with the set Novice
    Ask Generative Search questions grounded only in the Workspace.
  4. Add instructions Intermediate
    Tell the Workspace how you want answers framed for this project.
  5. Run a grid on the Workspace Intermediate
    Interrogate every document with the same questions.
  6. Return and extend Expert
    Reopen past chats, add new documents and build on earlier outputs.

Release notes

  
What's new

  

    
Last updatedOctober 26, 2026 · 10:30 AM ET

    
Changes sinceHow to use AlphaSense: interactive guide for consulting teams (version 1.0)

  

  

    
Version 2 · UX review updates
  • Personalize is now two screens: choose, then see your learning plan with a takeaway and where to start for your level.
  • The blue header appears on the first screen only.
  • Each feature is one page: no tabs inside tabs, and clickable Novice, Intermediate and Expert tabs on each step list.
  • Recommended features for your role always come first.
  • Coursework now has its own callout, and SuperAnalyst appears from the first screen.
  • The Your version view now shows a rough prompt, Enhance, and a competitor name.
  • The toolkit cards became a What's next section with AlphaSense IQ trainings.

    
    

      
Personalize Your Journey

      
  • A welcome overview now opens first, explaining the guide and the Learner's Journey and letting you choose your segment, role, industry and level. Skip it to use the general journey.
  • Fourteen personas across four segments: Corporate, Consulting, Financial services buy-side and Financial services sell-side.
  • Industry and level now sit together with the persona picker in one Personalize Your Journey tab.

    

    
    

      
Easier to navigate

      
  • The guide is split into tabs, one per stage, so you see one section at a time.
  • Each stage shows one feature at a time; pick the next feature from the buttons at the top of the stage.
  • A five-step guided tour, available from the top bar at any time.
  • Switch between Novice, Intermediate and Expert from the top bar. Every feature has Novice, Intermediate and Expert tabs on its step-by-step list.
  • Your choices and progress are saved in your browser, so returning visitors skip the welcome overview and continue where they left off.

    

    
    

      
Real screens, personalized

      
  • Every feature shows a real AlphaSense screenshot. Generative Search and SuperAnalyst also have a Your version view showing how the prompt for your persona and industry looks on that screen.
  • AlphaSense for PowerPoint and AlphaSense for Excel are now separate features, each with its own screenshot and steps.

    

    
    

      
Built around the Learner's Journey

      
  • Five stages: Getting answers fast, Going deeper, Scaling your work, Automating your work and Fitting into your workflows, covering 14 features.
  • Industry Comps and the Screener now sit within Financial Data; Keyword Search and Channel Checks are under Also in the toolkit.

    

    
    

      
Prompts

      
  • The prompt builder and the ready-made prompt library are one tab. Fill in the fields and click Generate prompt to see your prompt.
  • Ready-made prompts written for each persona and filled in for your industry.
  • Prompts are numbered to match their feature, with no gaps: features you use on screen rather than with a prompt (Workflow Agents, the Company Profile and the Mobile App) now come last in their stage.
  • Every ready-made prompt has been checked against what AlphaSense can do and shows where to run it. On-screen tasks, such as opening a Company Profile, launching a Workflow Agent or changing mobile settings, appear as steps rather than prompts.
